item.title: Reflections on My First Interview (as Interviewer)
item.description:
After being on the other side of the table many times, I finally got to conduct an interview myself. Although I’m still a junior developer, I still want to document this experience.

Overall, I didn’t speak at first, but when I noticed the candidate’s resume mentioned the TP framework and Yii framework, I couldn’t help asking a few questions about how these frameworks handle XSS and CSRF prevention.

When the conversation turned to how to determine whether two numbers in an array sum up to a target value, I asked a few more questions.

All in all, I’m fairly satisfied with my first interview. However, I might have been a bit too aggressive in my questioning. I should take note and work on improving that :).

item.title: Written on the Zeroth Anniversary of Graduation
item.description:
I’ve been so busy lately with graduation, moving, and starting a new job that I haven’t had a chance to sit down and write properly. I feel like I’ve become a full-fledged househusband - buying appliances, grocery shopping, cooking, getting takeout, doing housework, the whole nine yards.

I recently posted something on social media: “Once this door closes today, it’ll be two different worlds from now on.”

The zeroth anniversary of graduation marks the end of my 23-year student career (my mom says I started kindergarten at two and a half) and the beginning of year zero of my working life. Over the past year-plus of job hunting, I’ve been through the wringer - weathered all kinds of storms - but gradually got used to it.

What is growing up?

Growing up means:

  1. When you walk into a supermarket, you discover that even the cheapest bottle of cooking oil costs 30-40+ yuan; a single bowl costs 10 yuan. You learn to budget carefully.
  2. You boil an egg first thing in the morning.
  3. When cycling, don’t wear a backpack - it makes your back sweat like crazy. Just put it in the basket.
  4. You can tell the difference between electric bikes with removable lithium batteries and those with non-removable lead-acid batteries. The lithium battery ones don’t look as nice.
  5. You carefully observe Beijing’s elaborate transportation system and discover there are bike lanes with well-designed merging and diverging. Follow the bike lanes and you can ride smoothly to your destination, even through overpasses. This is probably a lot like life itself.
  6. You can soak the shower head in diluted disinfectant for effective sterilization.
  7. Yeah, I’m just broke.

I don’t know what the future holds. I’ve been wanting to learn Android development lately and check out the book “First Line of Code.” But whatever path lies ahead, I chose it, and I’ll see it through even if I have to crawl.

Finally, a note to myself: as long as your spirit never dies, life will keep running forward.

– DevHu, recorded on July 4, 2015, at a rented apartment.
